The greenback was at 100.40, up 0.15%, on Friday morning, with the index climbing from around 98.7 earlier in September, according to a chart. Barchart said the index was at its highest price since July and was on track for its eighth consecutive session without a lower close.

Earlier in the week, DXY advanced sharply after the Federal Reserve delivered a 25-basis-point increase in its benchmark interest rate. Investors had responded immediately by adding exposure to the greenback. Higher U.S. rates improve the relative yield on dollar assets, prompting a swift rotation into the currency.
